item.research_question: How can high-entropy alloy (HEA) nanoparticles be synthesized at low temperatures on conventional supports, and what mechanisms govern their formation and catalytic performance in CO2 hydrogenation?
item.material_system: CoNiCuRuPd high-entropy alloy nanoparticles supported on TiO2 (CoNiCuRuPd/TiO2); comparison with CoNiCuRuPd/Al2O3, CoNiCuRuPd/MgO, and monometallic Pd/TiO2, Ru/TiO2, Co/TiO2, Ni/TiO2, Cu/TiO2
item.processing_route: Simple impregnation of TiO2 with aqueous solutions of Co(NO3)2·6H2O, Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, Cu(NO3)2·3H2O, RuCl3·nH2O, and Na2PdCl4 (1:1:1:1:1 molar ratio; Pd 1.0 wt%); reduction under H2 flow (20 mL/min) at 400 °C for 2 h without prior calcination
item.test_conditions: CO2 hydrogenation at atmospheric pressure, 300–400 °C, with N2/H2/CO2 mixture (4/5/1 composition, total flow 50 mL/min, SV = 6000 mL/g/h); stability tested over 72 h; in situ XAFS and XRD under H2 at 200–400 °C; H2-TPR from 50 to 600 °C at 5 °C/min; CO-TPD and FTIR; TEM/STEM/EDX; ETEM under 300 kV electron beam; DFT and MD simulations at 900 K
key_findings: CoNiCuRuPd/TiO2 nanoparticles achieved an average size of 1.90 nm with a single-phase fcc structure (lattice parameter a = 3.734 Å), whereas CoNiCuRuPd/Al2O3 and CoNiCuRuPd/MgO yielded larger (6.65 and 6.73 nm), partially segregated particles.
The quinary-component precursors on TiO2 showed a single H2-TPR reduction peak at ~170 °C, indicating simultaneous reduction of all five metal ions, unlike broad peaks (130–250 °C) on Al2O3 and MgO.
CoNiCuRuPd/TiO2 exhibited 2–13 times higher yield of hydrogenated products than MgO and Al2O3 supports, with 68.3% CH4 selectivity at 400 °C.
The apparent activation energy for CO2 hydrogenation on CoNiCuRuPd/TiO2 was 37.7 kJ/mol, lower than 44.2 kJ/mol for Pd/TiO2.
After 72 h of reaction, CoNiCuRuPd/TiO2 retained 96% of its initial activity, while Pd/TiO2 dropped to 76% and Ru/TiO2 to 89%.
Particle growth was suppressed in CoNiCuRuPd/TiO2 (final diameter 2.3 nm) compared to Pd/TiO2 (final diameter 5.3 nm) after 72 h.

DFT calculations showed the cohesive energy of the HEA cluster (−3.92 eV) was higher than that of a pure Pd cluster (−3.09 eV), and diffusion coefficients in the HEA were ~1/3 lower than in pure Pd at 900 K.

CO adsorption on the HEA surface was stronger (Ead = −37.5 kcal/mol) than on pure Pd (−26.2 kcal/mol), shifting the CO stretching frequency from 2091 cm−1 (Pd/TiO2) to 2070 cm−1 (HEA/TiO2) and delaying desorption to >150 °C.
item.mechanism: The formation is driven by hydrogen spillover on TiO2: Pd2+ precursors are first reduced to form Pd nuclei; H2 dissociates on Pd to form Pd–H species; protons and electrons transfer to TiO2 lattice O2− anions, generating mobile H atoms that migrate rapidly over TiO2 via coupled proton/electron transfer, reducing all metal precursors simultaneously to form a solid-solution HEA. The sluggish diffusion and lattice distortion in the HEA enhance durability, while the cocktail effect (synergistic electronic properties) improves catalytic activity and CH4 selectivity by strengthening CO adsorption.
item.limitations: The study notes that the synthesis method was demonstrated only for the CoNiCuRuPd system and a few preliminary tests with Rh, Pt, and Au; applicability to other compositions requires further investigation. The text also mentions that monometallic Ru/TiO2 showed high activity but attributed it to extremely small particle size (0.89 nm), implying size effects must be controlled when comparing HEAs to monometallics.
item.future_work: The authors state that 'Further investigation to demonstrate the applicability of the present synthetic method is now under investigation' for other metal combinations (e.g., Rh, Pt, Au) and suggest the approach offers 'advanced insights into an innovative catalyst/photocatalyst architecture providing an essentially unlimited compositional space.'
quotes: This process is driven by the pronounced hydrogen spillover effect on TiO2 in conjunction with coupled proton/electron transfer.
CoNiCuRuPd HEA NPs on TiO2 produced in this work were found to be both active and extremely durable during the CO2 hydrogenation reaction.
The sluggish diffusion in these CoNiCuRuPd HEA NPs is caused by the combination of multiple metals, and that lattice distortion plays a crucial role in the superior robustness of this material.
